summary.headline: Suyog Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR710 mn (+6.1% YoY on electricity-inclusive basis), net profit INR145 mn; Vodafone Idea rollout began mid-June with 150 tenancies converted.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR710 mn, up 6.1% YoY against INR668 mn restated for electricity, with EBITDA of INR420 mn (59.3% margin) and PBT of INR195 mn. From 1 April the company began including electricity reimbursement in revenue after a GST-related guidance change, which lowered the reported EBITDA margin from about 70% to 59.3%. Vodafone Idea orders started flowing around 15-16 June; 95 towers (150 tenancies) were converted in June. Management said most growth will show from Q2 onwards, with the full benefit in FY28. Net profit margin was about 20% against 25% a year ago, which management attributed to a vendor-provision reversal in the prior-year quarter.

segments.name: Tower / IP1 infrastructure (India)
segments.commentary: Exit Q1 FY27 with 6,103 towers and 7,468 tenancies; tenancy ratio about 1.2x. Q1 additions were mainly macro sites, with a few kilometres of fibre laid.

segments.name: Fibre
segments.commentary: Management expects fibre at 5-8% of total revenue in FY27, with no major jump this year.

guidance_outlook: Target of 3,000 Vodafone Idea tenancies in FY27 (described as conservative); about 35-40% expected in H1 and 60% in H2. Management also cited ~850 tenancies in hand (150 done plus 700+ open).
Revenue per tower to be about INR31,000 ex-electricity; about INR50,000 per site with electricity per management's arithmetic.
EBITDA margin (with electricity) guided at around 59%, to be maintained in coming quarters; PAT margin to stay around 20%.

Management aims for INR100 crore quarterly revenue (INR400 crore annualised) from Q4 and PAT growth from ~22% to 24%, per the MD. The CFO flagged that Ind AS rent accounting mutes EBITDA margin in early years.
Tenancy ratio target of 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29.
Vodafone Idea FY28 target of about 5,000 further sites; Vodafone share of revenue targeted at 30-32% once the 3,000 sites are delivered.
capex_capacity: Zinc battery: sourced from GBB Batteries (Kerala plant) rather than manufactured in-house; first batch of 10-15 sites expected by mid-September, with a 100H unit at about INR33,000 vs INR48,000 for lithium (up ~50% in about 2.5 months).
Zinc battery expected to lower CapEx and some operating costs; management said it would be the first IP company in telecom to deploy it on sites.
Funding: management said internal accruals and bank funds cover the planned rollout. No fundraise decided; may come in Q2/Q3 if orders exceed plan.

BSNL: about 186 sites with pending billing from a prior ~1,000-site batch; expected to resume revenue in Q2 if Tejas equipment issues are resolved. No new BSNL projects booked until billing is confirmed.
demand_pricing: Vodafone Idea: about 45,000-site rollout plan over 18-24 months (3,000-3,500 per month); INR6,400 cr secured from SBI, with a further INR25,000-30,000 cr under discussion. Vodafone currently plans about 12,000 sites through September, and management expects roughly 30,000 in FY27.
Airtel and Jio not doing major rollouts per management. BSNL announced INR77,000 cr capex for 2 lakh sites over 5 years, but no new BSNL work is being taken until billing is confirmed.
Revenue share (per management): Airtel 48.1%, Vi 27%, Jio 22.6%, BSNL 2.3%.
MSAs with all operators are blanket frameworks with no fixed volume commitment; a 10-year lock-in with Vodafone was cited.
Sharing mix: 80% anchor and 20% shared on new Vodafone sites; macro sites carry tenancy ratios of 2-3x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the zinc battery project, its cost, and its margin and revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Zinc battery is bought from GBB Batteries, not manufactured in-house. Management said it cuts CapEx (100H unit at INR33,000 vs INR48,000 lithium) with no quantified EBITDA impact given.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence and breakdown of the 3,000 Vodafone tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident. It sees 850 tenancies in hand (150 done, 700+ open), expects 35-40% in H1 and 60% in H2, and says 80% will be on new towers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BSNL no longer being pushed in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not commit BSNL volumes until billing is confirmed. Tejas equipment issues have delayed BSNL rollouts by 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall from 25% to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year quarter included a vendor-provision reversal from Vi; management says the underlying margin is about 20-21% with electricity included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Vodafone target fall from 12,000 to about 10,500 tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3,000 figure is conservative and tied to funds already secured; the target will rise as Vodafone confirms more funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tenancy ratio path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ratio is about 1.2x; target is 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29, since macro sites carry 2-3 tenancies with recovery in 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are fibre's share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre is 5-8% of revenue and stays at that level in FY27; management says it is 100% recurring and carries a similar EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 189/186-site BSNL billing status?
qa_highlights.answer: 186 sites are still pending billing; management expects revenue from them to start in Q2.

risks_watch: Vodafone Idea funding: the 3,000-tenancy target depends on further SBI and consortium funds of INR25,000-30,000 cr; management says it will only raise its own targets once those are confirmed.
BSNL: 186 sites billing pending, Tejas equipment issues unresolved, and no firm rollout date.
Monsoon season may slow Q2 conversions.
Lithium battery costs up ~50% in 2.5 months; zinc battery first batch due mid-September and not yet proven on sites.
Funding: management is not ruling out a fundraise; the earlier call suggested one could come, and the analyst flagged this as an open question.
Margin optics: electricity reimbursement now in revenue, so margins are not comparable with prior periods, and the CFO flagged Ind AS rent accounting as muting EBITDA in early years.

key_quotes: We are very confident we'll achieve it because right now flow is very good.
So, 3,000 should not be a challenge for us.
But when I speak on a public platform where investors are there, what happens many times when we -- see we also commit based on the numbers which we receive from operator.
As of now, we have not decided whether not to go ahead with fundraise or when will we go ahead with fundraise.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Vodafone Idea pipeline and execution capacity, repeatedly calling the 3,000-tenancy FY27 target conservative and "not a challenge". Noticeably cautious and evasive on BSNL, declining to give volumes or dates until billing and Tejas equipment issues are resolved, and on fundraising, which is undecided.

adds.what: 3,000 additional Vodafone Idea tenancies in FY27 (conservative target; ~35-40% in H1, 60% in H2)
Zinc battery first batch of 10-15 sites (sourced from GBB Batteries, not in-house)
Vodafone Idea FY28 target of about 5,000 further sites

growth.why: Management guides 3,000 Vodafone Idea tenancies in FY27 (about 850 in hand, 7,000+ existing, 10,000+ exit) and an INR100 cr quarterly revenue target from Q4 FY27, but Q1 revenue grew only 6.1% YoY on an electricity-inclusive basis, revenue per tower is flat at INR31,000-31,500, and most growth is expected from Q2 onward.
